surprises.description: Dorman narrowed its FY2026 sales-growth outlook to 2%–3%, below the preview’s expected narrowing to roughly 3%–4%. It also lowered the top of its adjusted EPS range from $8.80 to $8.70 rather than holding the prior range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was narrowed to net sales growth of 2% to 3% and adjusted diluted EPS of $8.50 to $8.70 (tightened from $8.50-$8.80), reflecting soft DIY demand and tariff-related price reductions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Best outcome: trim revenue to 3–4%, raise or hold adj. EPS $8.50–$8.80”; the preview’s base case also expected the EPS band to be maintained.

surprises.description: Heavy-duty sales grew, but the segment operated at breakeven margin despite the preview’s focus on a margin inflection and its reference to 4.2% operating margin in Q2. Higher tariff and shipping costs, with heavier tariff effects still expected later in 2026, left the segment weaker than that inflection setup suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Heavy-duty net sales rose about 5% to $66 million but operated at breakeven margin due to higher tariff and shipping costs, with the heavier tariff impact expected later in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Heavy Duty operating margin inflection”; the preview cited 4.2% in Q2'26 and said management expected second-half growth above the company average.

surprises.description: Light-duty sales grew about 3%, below the preview’s mid-single-digit Q3 growth threshold for the volume-led thesis. DIFM was stable, but continued DIY pressure limited the segment’s growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Light-duty net sales grew about 3% to $444 million”; “DIFM stable while DIY remained pressured.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Mid-single-digit Light Duty growth in Q3 with positive volume = thesis intact.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $2.08 exceeded the preview’s $2.00 consensus estimate and its $1.97 alternative, despite falling year over year. The expected decline was about 24%–25%, versus the reported 21% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS fell 21% to $2.08 from $2.62 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $2.00” and “Adj. diluted EPS (alt.) $1.97”; the preview listed implied year-over-year declines of 23.7% and 24.8%.

surprises.description: Sales were slightly below both preview consensus estimates: $562 million versus $565.3 million and the alternative $563.1 million. The reported roughly 3% growth was also below the consensus-implied 3.6%–4.0% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 consolidated net sales reached a record $562 million, up approximately 3% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales $565.3M” and “Net sales (alt.) $563.1M”; the preview listed implied year-over-year growth of 4.0% and 3.6%.

surprises.description: Gross margin came in at 39.4%, modestly above the preview’s implied range of roughly 38.5%–39.0%. It cleared the preview’s 39% catalyst, although the result remained below the roughly 40% Q4 level management was expected to reach.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin declined 500 basis points year-over-year to 39.4%,” with management guiding to “roughly 40% gross margin in Q4 as a structural base entering 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Gross margin: ~38.5–39.0%” and identified “Gross margin ≥ 39%” as its primary catalyst.
